page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 architecture, driven by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the m7a.8xlarge in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core CPU execution via stress-ng and Geekbench. It demonstrates strong capabilities in specialized tasks, scoring in the top 25% for software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory performance is robust, with DDR5 memory bandwidth for small block reads and large block writes ranking in the top 25%, though large block read bandwidth and Passmark memory scores fall into the middle 50%. Notably, it achieves top-tier status in LLM inference prompt processing for small models, alongside strong text generation speeds for medium models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory deliver strong resource density and high performance-per-vCPU without the overhead of hyperthreading. This makes the instance highly suitable for compute-heavy general-purpose workloads, database operations, software development, and light LLM inference tasks.
